title: Settlement Agreements Consumer Action Card: Signing a Hardship Settlement Electronically
content:
# Hardship Settlement — Acceptance by Electronic Signature

## Subject of the rule

This rule fixes the Hardship Settlement signing window, the number of calendar days from the acceptance date to the due date of the first settlement payment, when a consumer accepts a Hardship Settlement offer by electronic signature, the way a Hardship Settlement is accepted because it cannot be accepted on a recorded call; acceptance of any other programme is outside this rule. The Hardship Settlement is a programme of Ridgeline's Settlement Agreements.

## What the signature waits on

An electronically signed acceptance of a Hardship Settlement is booked only after the account carries an open Hardship Settlement offer dated within its validity.

Said the other way round: so long as the account shows no Hardship Settlement offer in status offered and within its validity on the handling date, no electronically signed acceptance of a Hardship Settlement is booked.

## What the consumer's action does

`sign_settlement_offer_electronically_52f226cb` is the consumer's electronic signature on an open written settlement offer on one of their placed accounts. One call moves that settlement from offered to accepted with today as the acceptance date and an electronic signature as the acceptance method, sets the first settlement payment due the given number of calendar days after today and the final payment due the offer's payment interval after it for each remaining payment, sets the amount still to pay under the settlement to the offer's settlement amount, and books that settlement amount to the settlement once as today's scheduled amount. The consumer can see the settlement as accepted with its new due dates.

## How it is invoked

The consumer's own tool: the agent unlocks `sign_settlement_offer_electronically_52f226cb` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it.

## Parameters

- `settlement_id` — identifier: the settlement reference number of the open offer being signed, as returned by the settlement lookup.
- `first_payment_due_in_days` — whole integer of at least 1: the number of calendar days after today on which settlement payment 1 falls due.

## Return

A text rendering of a dictionary with `settlement_id`, `status` (always "accepted" on success), `accepted_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, today), `acceptance_method` (`e_signature`), `first_payment_due_date` and `final_payment_due_date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `amount_scheduled` (USD, 2 decimals, the settlement amount booked today) and `schedule_entry_id` (reference of the booked scheduled-amount entry). A returned status of accepted means the acceptance is on record.

## Hypothetical receipt

Signed with a hypothetical settlement reference and a value of 20 for `first_payment_due_in_days`, on an offer with three payments 30 days apart, the receipt shows status accepted, method `e_signature`, a first payment due 20 calendar days after today and a final payment due 80 calendar days after today.
